Recommendation: keep [PR #1951](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1951) open, fix its blockers, then merge it. Don’t close it in favor of documentation alone, but don’t merge the current head.

## Findings

### High: the legacy-origin fallback does not reliably find legacy checkpoints

The implementation chooses metadata at branch/ref granularity, not checkpoint granularity:

- The fetch loop stops as soon as the elected remote has any metadata branch: [git_operations.go](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/fix-checkpoint-read-remotes/cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go:407>).
- Reads then search only that selected tree and return “not found” if the requested checkpoint is absent: [persistent.go](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/fix-checkpoint-read-remotes/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:1351>).
- Tracking-ref fallback occurs only when the local read ref is missing: [persistent.go](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/fix-checkpoint-read-remotes/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:2198>).

This breaks two realistic states:

1. The elected upstream has newer checkpoints, while an older requested checkpoint exists only on origin.
2. `EnsurePrimaryRef` creates an empty local orphan because upstream lacks a tracking ref; that orphan then shadows origin entirely: [common.go](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/fix-checkpoint-read-remotes/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:609>).

The integration test misses this because it deletes the local primary and both tracking refs before testing fallback: [checkpoint_read_remotes_test.go](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/fix-checkpoint-read-remotes/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/checkpoint_read_remotes_test.go:31>).

Fix: make git-branch fallback sensitive to the requested checkpoint—or explicitly reconcile candidate metadata histories—then test both an existing local orphan and an elected branch that exists but lacks the origin-only checkpoint.

### Medium: cross-repo callers can resolve candidates from the wrong repository

`reviewCommittedCheckpointContext` opens `worktreeRoot` but resolves settings/remotes through the ambient context: [review_context.go](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/fix-checkpoint-read-remotes/cmd/entire/cli/review_context.go:92>).

Dispatch creates `repoCtx`, but the underlying election still executes unscoped `git config` and `git remote` commands: [checkpoint_sync_remote.go](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/fix-checkpoint-read-remotes/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go:119>), [manual_commit_push.go](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/fix-checkpoint-read-remotes/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:240>).

Fix: make remote election explicitly repository-root-aware and use the repo-scoped context consistently for store operations.

## Product judgment

The “close it and add a warning” option is too weak as the final resolution:

- #1893 already advertises `checkpoint_push_remote` as the supported fork configuration.
- Non-origin election also happens naturally in origin-less repositories; it is not limited to users of an obscure setting.
- After #1956, git-refs checkpoints can become visible in listings but remain unhydratable. That is a particularly confusing partial feature.
- Of the 2,110 added lines, 1,437 are tests and only 643 are production code. The change is still large, but the raw total exaggerates its runtime footprint.

A hydration-only split does not avoid most of the difficult work: metadata branches, per-checkpoint refs, blob fetching, local-ref confinement, and both backends still need coherent candidate semantics.

So the actionable decision is:

1. Merge #1956 independently if its own review is clean.
2. Hold #1951 at current head.
3. Fix the two issues above—especially checkpoint-level legacy fallback.
4. Re-run review and merge #1951 rather than replacing it with permanent documentation of broken read-back.
5. A status warning is useful as an interim safeguard, not as the final product behavior.
